chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Safwan, from al-Ala', from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said:
I asked him about the man who turns (his head) during the prayer. He said: No (it does not break the prayer), nor does he break (crack) his fingers.
ai.seo_question: What actions during prayer do not break the validity of salat?
ai.summary: In this concise ruling from Imam al-Sadiq (AS), the specific actions of turning the head (al-iltifāt) and cracking fingers are distinguished from major invalidators, reflecting the Shia juristic principle that minor, non-distracting movements do not break the prayer's validity. This hadith is frequently cited in discussions on *sunan al-salat* (voluntary acts) versus *mubtilat* (invalidators), emphasizing that only significant gestures or laughter that distract from devotion nullify the prayer. It underscores the practical ease (*taysir*) in Shia fiqh regarding bodily movements during worship.
